nativeValidation.platform: Windows with a macOS fallback for symlink-capable case-insensitive validation
nativeValidation.setup: Run in PowerShell from the matching repository checkout on a case-insensitive volume. Record the actual checkout SHA and both fixture capability logs. When both process contexts are available, rerun the last command from a context with the opposite symlink capability and save its output under a distinct name.
expectedResults: The separator fixture reports that the two spellings map to one local path. Both archive orders with an absent and an existing destination return failed_precondition with both original names. The previous destination state remains, and local staging and the fixture guest archive are removed.
On a case-insensitive volume, the regular-only case collision and the regular-first mixed case collision return failed_precondition with both original names and preserve both destination states.
When the process can create a symlink, the mixed symlink-first case gives the same failure and cleanup. The exact-name mixed fixtures pass in both orders.

When the process cannot create a symlink, the mixed regular-first case still gives the collision error. The noncolliding link produces the warning and preserves both regular files. The reverse-order fixture skips because it cannot stage a symlink.
The optional ./ prefix continues to allow the last regular entry for a repeated archive name to replace its predecessor.

macosFallback.setup: Run from the matching checkout on case-insensitive APFS with symlink support if the Windows process cannot create symlinks. The separator case itself requires Windows.
expectedResults: The probe reports case-sensitive: false and symlink creation: true. Both mixed orders and both destination states pass with failed_precondition, both archive names, preserved destinations and cleanup.
The regular-only case collision and exact-name mixed replacement fixtures also pass.
